It depends on what kind of protection you are really looking for. There are also certainly options for phones outside of ios, android, wp, blackberry. Going with a feature phone would give you a much smaller attack vector than an android phone filled with tons of bloatware apps.

If you are concerned with apps leaking random information for marketing etc then you should do a factory reset on your phone and don't install any apps with shady permissions. The flashlight app that wants access to your contact list? Don't allow it and get a different one instead.

Concerned about your files getting leaked? Stop using cloud services and use alternative apps instead. Did you know DropBox had a period of time where you could literally type in ANY password along with a legitimate user name to gain full access to an account? You could always do the archaic manual copying of a file.

If you are concerned about your carrier eavesdropping on what you are doing then you need to use some sort of encryption between you and the other end. You could setup a VPN on your phone and by default encrypt ALL of your data traffic to your cell provider. Alternatively you could use specific apps with integrated encryption (like silent circle or many others). If you want back and forth communication with another person this will require them to be encrypting their side as well or it is all pointless.

Keep in mind if you are using third party programs or VPNs then you would be reliant on yet another 3rd party/middle man for privacy. Really, if you are very concerned with tracking or privacy owning a cellphone in the first place, let alone a smart phone, is probably not a good choice.

Many would make the case that freedom & privacy cannot exist as long as you are running closed source (non-free, Free as in freedom) software. This based on the fact that you can NEVER know what is in the code. http://www.fsf.org/
